headline: This 2015 law lets the VA spend up to $900 million to replace the Denver VA Medical Center and widens when veterans may use non-VA medical facilities under the veterans choice program.
what_it_does: It authorizes the Department of Veterans Affairs to replace the existing VA Medical Center in Denver, Colorado, in fiscal year 2015, with spending capped at $900 million. It also changes how the 40-mile distance rule in the veterans choice program is applied. Under the change, a veteran may use a non-VA facility if they live more than 40 driving miles from the closest VA facility, or if traveling to a VA facility is an unusual or excessive burden. That burden can come from geography, road access, traffic, hazardous weather, a medical condition that affects travel, or other factors the Secretary decides.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans in Denver and the surrounding area
who_it_affects.how: They are served by the Denver VA Medical Center, which the law authorizes the VA to replace.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans who live more than 40 driving miles from a VA facility
who_it_affects.how: They may be able to get care at a non-VA medical facility under the veterans choice program.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans facing travel burdens such as poor road access, hazardous weather, or medical conditions that make travel hard
who_it_affects.how: They may qualify to use a non-VA facility even if they live within 40 miles of a VA facility.
It is authorized to spend up to $900 million on the Denver facility and to apply the expanded travel-burden standard when deciding whether veterans may use non-VA care.

when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not state a separate effective date for these provisions. The law was enacted on May 22, 2015, and the Denver authorization refers to fiscal year 2015.
